title: Shopify Horizon Theme — Design System Architecture Overview
content: Analysis of Shopify's Horizon theme (v3.5.1) — their next-generation flagship theme and the reference implementation for modern Shopify design systems. Horizon is NOT eligible for Theme Store (use Skeleton for that) but represents Shopify's vision for how themes should be built. CORE PHILOSOPHY: (1) Web-native — built on evergreen web standards with progressive enhancement, no polyfills. (2) Performance-focused — features ship only when lean, fast, and reliable. (3) Server-rendered — HTML via Liquid, business logic on Shopify servers, not client-side. (4) Functional design — semantic markup, progressive enhancement, cross-browser without pixel-perfect demands. LANGUAGE COMPOSITION: 72.9% Liquid, 23.0% JavaScript, 4.1% CSS. This ratio is key — the theme is overwhelmingly Liquid-first with minimal JS. CSS is also minimal because tokens are generated dynamically via Liquid snippets. ARCHITECTURE: Directory follows standard Shopify structure (assets, blocks, config, layout, locales, sections, snippets, templates). The design system is NOT a static CSS file — it is a Liquid-powered token generation system. Tokens are defined in settings_schema.json (merchant-configurable), rendered as CSS custom properties by Liquid snippets (theme-styles-variables.liquid, color-schemes.liquid, typography-style.liquid, spacing-style.liquid, gap-style.liquid), and consumed by a single base.css file plus component-level styles. COMPONENT COUNT: 41 sections, 127 blocks (51 private/helper prefixed with _, 76 public), 90+ snippets. This is a block-heavy architecture — blocks are the primary unit of composition, not sections. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Mirror this architecture. Your Figma design system should have a variables layer (matching settings_schema.json), a token layer (matching the CSS custom properties), and a component layer (matching blocks). Sections in Figma are compositions of blocks, not monolithic designs.

title: Shopify Horizon — Token Architecture & CSS Custom Properties
content: Deep analysis of Horizon's token system. Tokens are NOT static — they are dynamically generated via Liquid snippets that read from settings_schema.json and output CSS custom properties on :root. TOKEN GENERATION PIPELINE: settings_schema.json (merchant settings) → Liquid snippets → CSS custom properties → base.css + component styles. KEY TOKEN FILES: (1) theme-styles-variables.liquid — the master token file. Generates 200+ CSS custom properties covering layout, typography, colours, spacing, borders, animations, z-index, and component-specific tokens. (2) color-schemes.liquid — generates colour scheme tokens per scheme, with brightness-based opacity adjustment (dark backgrounds get higher opacity values: 0.15/0.25/0.55/0.60 vs light: 0.05/0.10/0.35/0.40). (3) typography-style.liquid — generates font tokens with fluid scaling via clamp() for sizes ≥3rem. Auto-classifies text as 'display' (>4.5rem), 'heading' (>3.5rem), or 'body'. (4) spacing-style.liquid — generates responsive padding with scaling. Values >20px use max() with calc(var(--spacing-scale) * value) for fluid responsive spacing. Values ≤20px are fixed. (5) gap-style.liquid — generates responsive gap tokens. Values >24px scale with --gap-scale multiplier (default 1.0), values ≤24px are fixed. LAYOUT TOKENS: --sidebar-width, --narrow-content-width, --normal-content-width, --wide-content-width, --narrow-page-width, --normal-page-width, --wide-page-width. Page margin: 16px mobile, 40px at ≥750px. COLOUR TOKENS: Static colours: --color-error (#8B0000), --color-success (#006400), --color-white (#FFFFFF), --color-black (#000000), --color-instock (#3ED660), --color-lowstock (#EE9441), --color-outofstock (#C8C8C8). Dynamic colours per scheme: --color-foreground, --color-background, --color-heading, --color-primary, --color-primary-hover, --color-shadow, plus button/input/variant/border variants. OPACITY SCALE: --opacity-5 through --opacity-90 with combined values (--opacity-5-15, --opacity-10-25, --opacity-35-55, --opacity-40-60, --opacity-subdued-text). Z-INDEX LAYERS: --layer-flat, --layer-raised, --layer-sticky, --layer-section-background, --layer-lowest (range -2 to 20). ANIMATION TOKENS: Easing functions (cubic-bezier variations), duration speeds (fast/medium/slow), spring animations with perceptual duration. Hover tokens: --hover-lift-amount (4px), --hover-scale-amount (1.03), --hover-subtle-zoom-amount (1.015), --hover-transition-duration (0.25s). FIGMA IMPLICATION: Set up Figma variables to match this token structure. Create variable collections for: Colours (with light/dark modes matching colour schemes), Typography (with fluid type scale), Spacing (matching the spacing scale from 3xs to 6xl), Layout (page widths), and Animation (for prototype transitions). The opacity scale is unusually granular — replicate it for consistent transparency usage.
source: github.com/Shopify/horizon — snippets/theme-styles-variables.liquid, color-schemes.liquid, typography-style.liquid, spacing-style.liquid, gap-style.liquid

title: Shopify Horizon — Colour System & Scheme Architecture
content: Horizon's colour system is scheme-based and brightness-aware. COLOUR SCHEMES: Defined in settings_schema.json, each scheme contains: background, foreground, heading, text, primary (+ hover), border, shadow, plus full button token sets (primary/secondary/tertiary with text, background, border, hover variants), input tokens, variant picker tokens, selected variant tokens, and disabled input tokens. Muted foreground and per-heading colours (h1-h6) are also configurable per scheme. BRIGHTNESS DETECTION: The system calculates background brightness and adjusts opacity values automatically. Dark backgrounds (brightness < 64): opacity values 0.15, 0.25, 0.55, 0.60, 0.60. Light backgrounds (brightness ≥ 64): opacity values 0.05, 0.10, 0.35, 0.40, 0.30. This creates correct visual hierarchy regardless of scheme — shadows are more visible on dark, less on light. CONDITIONAL SHADOWS: --shadow-drawer applied only when settings.drawer_drop_shadow is enabled. --shadow-popover and --shadow-blur applied only when settings.popover_drop_shadow is enabled. STATIC COLOURS (not scheme-dependent): Error red (#8B0000), success green (#006400), white (#FFFFFF), black (#000000), in-stock green (#3ED660), low-stock orange (#EE9441), out-of-stock grey (#C8C8C8). RGB VARIANTS: Key colours also expose RGB channels (--color-foreground-rgb, --color-shadow-rgb, --color-white-rgb) for use with rgba() and opacity adjustments. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Create a Figma variable collection called 'Colour Schemes' with modes for each scheme (e.g. Scheme 1 Light, Scheme 1 Dark, Scheme 2, etc.). Map every colour token as a variable. The static colours (error, success, stock status) should be in a separate 'System Colours' collection with no modes — they are constant. Use the RGB variants to create opacity-adjusted colour styles. The brightness-based opacity adjustment is elegant — replicate it by creating opacity variable sets that swap between light and dark modes.

title: Shopify Horizon — Typography System & Fluid Scaling
content: Horizon's typography system supports four font families with fluid responsive scaling. FONT FAMILIES: (1) Primary/body font — used for paragraph text. (2) Secondary/subheading font — used for subheadings and labels. (3) Tertiary/heading font — used for h1-h6 headings. (4) Accent font — used for decorative/brand text. Each font loads bold, italic, and bold-italic variants. Duplicate @font-face declarations are prevented by tracking rendered fonts in a string variable. HEADING TOKENS: Each heading level (h1-h6) has independently configurable: font choice (from the 4 families), size (10-184px range), line height, letter spacing, text case. This means h1 can use the accent font while h2 uses the heading font — maximum flexibility. FLUID SCALING: Sizes ≥3rem use clamp() for fluid typography relative to a 1400px target viewport. The formula calculates a viewport-width percentage so type scales smoothly between breakpoints. Sizes <3rem are fixed. AUTO-CLASSIFICATION: The system auto-assigns text type based on size: >4.5rem = 'display' type, >3.5rem = 'heading' type, below = 'body' type. Each type gets different line-height and letter-spacing presets. PARAGRAPH: Configurable size range 10-18px with its own family, style, weight, line-height, letter-spacing, and case settings. BUTTON TYPOGRAPHY: Separate font-family and text-case tokens for buttons (--button-font-family, --button-text-case), allowing buttons to use a different font from body text. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Create a Figma variable collection for Typography with variables for each heading level's size, line-height, letter-spacing, weight, and family. Create text styles for: paragraph, h1-h6, subheading, accent, and button. For fluid type, set up responsive variants using Figma's min/max width settings on text. The 4-font-family system means your Figma font stack needs 4 font slots — do not assume heading and body use the same font. Design each heading level as independently configurable in your component properties.

title: Shopify Horizon — Spacing Scale, Layout System & Responsive Scaling
content: Horizon's spacing and layout system uses responsive scaling with minimum thresholds. SPACING SCALE: Variables from --margin-3xs through --margin-6xl and --padding-xs through --padding-3xl, plus --gap-2xs through --gap (and custom named gaps). Spacing values >20px scale responsively using max(min, calc(var(--spacing-scale) * valuepx)). Values ≤20px are fixed pixel values. This ensures small spacing stays crisp while large spacing compresses on smaller screens. GAP SYSTEM: Gap values >24px scale with --gap-scale multiplier (default 1.0). Values ≤24px are fixed. The gap-style snippet generates a single --gap (or custom-named) CSS property per component. LAYOUT WIDTHS: Three page width options: narrow, normal, wide. Content widths: --narrow-content-width, --normal-content-width, --wide-content-width. Page widths: --narrow-page-width, --normal-page-width, --wide-page-width. PAGE MARGIN: 16px on mobile, 40px at ≥750px breakpoint. SECTION SIZING: --section-min-height and --section-height-offset for full-height and constrained sections. FLEX LAYOUT: layout-panel-style.liquid generates flex tokens: --flex-direction (default column), --flex-wrap (nowrap desktop, wrap mobile), --horizontal-alignment, --vertical-alignment, --vertical-alignment-mobile (with baseline→flex-end mobile override). RESPONSIVE APPROACH: Horizon does NOT use traditional CSS Grid columns. Instead it uses flex-based layouts with responsive gap scaling and content-width constraints. The page width acts as max-width container. Content sections sit inside the page width, full-bleed sections span the viewport. ICON SIZES: --icon-size-2xs, --icon-size-xs, --icon-size-sm, --icon-size-md. TOUCH TARGET: --minimum-touch-target (maps to 44px accessibility requirement). FIGMA IMPLICATION: Create a spacing variable collection with values matching the 3xs-6xl scale. Use auto layout in Figma with gap values from this scale. For page layout, set up frames at the three width options (narrow, normal, wide) plus full-bleed. The flex-first approach means your Figma layouts should rely heavily on auto layout with wrap and gap — not fixed grid columns. This is a shift from the Dawn/traditional Shopify grid approach.

title: Shopify Horizon — Block-First Component Architecture & Naming
content: Horizon uses a block-first architecture that is fundamentally different from Dawn and older themes. BLOCK-FIRST: 127 blocks vs 41 sections. Blocks are the primary compositional unit. Sections are containers that host blocks. This inverts the Dawn model where sections contained most logic. BLOCK NAMING: Private/helper blocks are prefixed with underscore (e.g. _product-card, _card, _heading, _image, _content, _divider). 51 private blocks, 76 public blocks. Private blocks are internal implementation details not directly added by merchants. Public blocks are the merchant-facing building blocks. PUBLIC BLOCK CATEGORIES: Purchase flow — add-to-cart, buy-buttons, price, quantity, variant-picker, swatches, accelerated-checkout. Product info — product-title, product-description, product-inventory, product-custom-property, sku, review. Content — text, heading (via _heading), image, video, icon, button, spacer, divider, custom-liquid, page-content, page. Layout — group (flex container for other blocks). Navigation — menu, logo, collection-title. Commerce — product-card, collection-card, featured-collection, product-recommendations, filters. Forms — contact-form, contact-form-submit-button, email-signup. Social — social-links, follow-on-shop. Footer — footer-copyright, footer-policy-list, payment-icons. Interactive — accordion, comparison-slider, jumbo-text, popup-link. SECTION CATEGORIES: Page templates — main-404, main-blog, main-blog-post, main-cart, main-collection, main-collection-list, main-page. Content — hero, slideshow, layered-slideshow, carousel, marquee, media-with-content, divider, custom-liquid, section. Product — product-information, featured-product, featured-product-information, product-hotspots, product-list, product-recommendations, quick-order-list. Commerce — collection-links, collection-list. Blog — featured-blog-posts. Navigation — header, header-announcements, footer, footer-utilities, predictive-search, predictive-search-empty, search-header, search-results. Layout — _blocks (private), section, logo. Auth — password, password-footer. SECTION GROUPS: header-group.json and footer-group.json — persistent across all pages. KEY SNIPPETS: product-card.liquid, button.liquid, swatch.liquid, price.liquid, image.liquid — these are the reusable rendering primitives that blocks delegate to. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Structure your Figma component library to match this hierarchy: (1) Primitives layer — matches snippets (button, image, price, swatch, icon). (2) Blocks layer — matches public blocks (add-to-cart, variant-picker, product-card, etc.). Each block is a component. (3) Sections layer — matches sections. Each section is a component composed of blocks. (4) Templates layer — matches template types. Each template is a frame composed of sections. Use the underscore naming convention for internal-only components in Figma (prefix with _ or place in a 'Private' page).

title: Shopify Horizon — Settings Schema & Merchant Configuration
content: Horizon's settings_schema.json defines all merchant-configurable design tokens. This is the source of truth that drives the entire design system — every visual decision flows from here. SETTING GROUPS: (1) Logo & Favicon — logo image, inverse logo, desktop height (12-100px), mobile height (12-100px), favicon. (2) Colour Schemes — full colour token set per scheme: background, foreground, heading, text, primary + hover, border, shadow, button sets (primary/secondary/tertiary with text/bg/border/hover), input colours, variant colours, selected variant colours, disabled input colours, muted foreground, heading colours (h1-h6), optional shadows. (3) Typography — 4 font selections (body, subheading, heading, accent). Paragraph size (10-18px). Each heading level (h1-h6) independently configurable: font choice, size (10-184px), line height, letter spacing, text case. (4) Page Layout — width options: narrow, normal, wide. (5) Animations — page transitions toggle, product transitions, cart animation toggle, card hover effect (none, lift, scale, subtle-zoom). (6) Badges — position, border radius, colours. (7) Buttons — primary/secondary styling, pill mode, text case. (8) Cart — type (drawer/page), pricing display, features, thumbnail config. (9) Drawers — colour scheme, borders, shadows. (10) Icons — stroke weight. (11) Input Fields — borders, border radius. (12) Popovers/Modals — styling. (13) Prices — currency code visibility. (14) Product Cards — quick add toggle, carousel toggle. (15) Search — configuration. (16) Swatches — sizing, borders, border radius. (17) Variant Pickers — styling. FIGMA IMPLICATION: This settings schema IS your Figma variable architecture. Create a Figma variable collection for each setting group. Every setting with a default value becomes a Figma variable with that default. Colour scheme settings become modes. Typography settings become text style definitions. The settings schema is the contract between designer and developer — when your Figma variables match settings_schema.json, developer handoff is trivial because the mapping is 1:1.
